headline: Majors rest at extreme overbought levels after three-week rally; whales moving coins onto exchanges while crowd sentiment peaks at greed.
paragraphs: The regime across majors is unified but stretched. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages, yet none has achieved a golden cross, meaning the 50-day has not reclaimed the 200-day. That absence matters: the uptrend is steep but young. The seven-day picture is emphatic: Bitcoin up 22.2% on the week, Ethereum up 30.4%, Solana up 33.4%, and XRP up 40.2%. Over 30 days the numbers barely compress, confirming the rally is not a one-day flush but a sustained move. Yet on the day, every single asset in the major six is down: Bitcoin down 0.3%, Ethereum down 0.5%, Solana down 0.7%, XRP down 1.2%, BNB down 0.8%, and Doge down 0.8%. This intra-day pullback off a three-week sprint is the first texture worth noting: momentum has not broken, but it has paused.

Momentum indicators confirm the pause, not a reversal. RSI-14 across the board sits in the extreme overbought zone: Bitcoin at 79.5, Ethereum at 76.0, Solana at 80.6, BNB at 76.7, XRP at 69.9. When RSI hits 70 and stays, it tells you the crowd is exhausted in the upward direction; when it hits 80, the muscle has stopped firing. All four majors are there or near it. MACD remains above signal line for every asset, so the directional bias has not turned, but MACD itself is a lagging measure and does not warn of a breakdown before it happens. The combination reads as: the trend is intact but the sellers have arrived after a big move and are testing the high-water mark. Doge and ADA, the weaker names, sit below their 200-day lines despite weekly gains, a divergence that suggests the rally may be concentrating in the tier-one names.

Derivatives positioning shows crowded longs at expensive funding. Bitcoin funding on OKX trades at 0.67% per eight hours, or annualized 7.3%, a meaningful carry but not panic-level high. Ethereum sits at 0.01 per eight hours (11% annualized), which is materially hotter and signals longs are willing to pay to hold after the 30% week. Open interest on Bitcoin is $2.28 billion and on Ethereum $1.60 billion; both figures are substantial but not historically extreme. More revealing is the long-to-short ratio: Bitcoin at 1.11-to-1 and Ethereum at 1.10-to-1 show modest long bias, not crowded extremes. XRP and especially Doge skew harder long (XRP at 2.36-to-1, Doge at 3.67-to-1), a sign that retail and leveraged accounts have compressed into those names during the bounce. Liquidations in the last 24 hours show 1,399 total on Bitcoin with longs taking 55% of the pain, and 1,600 on Ethereum with shorts taking the majority (1600 count, 8.5M in short liquidations versus 6.4M in long), a mixed picture that suggests neither side is being systematically cleaned out but rather the market is shaking weak hands on both flanks.

Whale flows reveal the most important friction: $170 million net of Ethereum moved onto exchanges in the past 24 hours, the entirety of that directed to Coinbase institutional desks. Bitcoin saw $181 million inflow offset by $181 million outflow, netting essentially flat on the day, but the weekly picture is severe: $1.42 billion moved onto exchanges in the week ending August 27, the largest weekly inflow in three weeks. The prior week of August 20 saw only $19 million onto exchanges, so the acceleration from June levels is sharp. Coinbase institutional has been the primary receiver of these deposits across all three major inflows on the list. This pattern, combined with the daily pullback and extreme overbought RSI, suggests large accounts are taking chips off the table after the 30-plus percent rally. The message is not capitulation; it is profit-taking into institutional bid.

Sentiment sits at 71 on the Fear and Greed index, labeled Greed, and it has ranged from 25 to 74 over the past month. The crowd is confident after three weeks of gains, yet the tape says the tape is at rest. Stablecoin float stands at $309.2 billion, up just 0.75% over 30 days, indicating dry powder has not meaningfully dried up and is available if dip-buyers need it. Total market cap fell 2.55% in the last 24 hours while Bitcoin dominance held at 59.1%, showing weakness spread across the board rather than rotation out of Bitcoin. Spot ETF inflows have persisted for 8 consecutive days in both Bitcoin and Ethereum, with Bitcoin at $232 million on August 26 and Ethereum at $192 million, suggesting traditional finance continues to nibble. The gap between what the tape shows (coins moving to exchange deposits, RSI at 80, daily pullback) and what the sentiment gauge reports (greed at 71) is the day's central tension: institutional calm during retail confidence.

Watch for two conditions: first, whether RSI on Bitcoin and Ethereum breaks below 60 on a two-day close, which would signal momentum has shifted from overbought pause to directional reversal. Second, monitor whether the weekly whale flow reverses direction, moving back off exchanges, which would indicate the institutional profit-taking is done and dry powder is deploying again into this rally. Until either condition appears, the read is simple: a three-week rally has exhausted momentum in the near term, large accounts are trimming, and the crowd is still congratulating itself. Doge and ADA remain below their 200-day lines, a warning flag for the lower tier.
